subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Framing Effects
description: A micro-lesson that makes Framing Effects usable.

hook.text: A surgery has a 90% survival rate. The same surgery has a 10% death rate.

buildup.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that framing changes choices dramatically.

discovery.text: Marketers use framing daily. '95% fat-free' sells better than '5% fat.' The information is identical.

twist.text: Framing affects experts too. Judges give different sentences for the same crime based on how the case description is.

climax.text: Framing shows that human preferences are not fixed. The same options presented differently produce different choices.

punchline.text: Same facts, different frame, different choice.

quiz.question: What does the framing effect demonstrate?
options: Identical information presented differently leads to different decisions
